activities.name: Computer Science Research at State University Lab

rationale.intuition: MIT overall ~4.5%, EA admit ~5.2%, RD ~3.8%. Undocumented/DACA-recipient applicants are evaluated identically to domestic applicants at MIT — MIT is need-blind for undocumented students and meets full demonstrated need (per MIT financial aid policy). First-gen + strong STEM (USACO Gold + Regeneron STS) is the real lifting hook here; undocumented status is policy-neutral at MIT specifically (would be need-aware at some peers). Counselor consensus 8-22% for strong first-gen STEM applicant; undocumented status itself adds zero direct lift at MIT but constrains school list to need-blind-for-undocumented schools.

sources.name: MIT Financial Aid Policy 2024
sources.evidence: MIT is need-blind for all admitted applicants regardless of citizenship status, including undocumented and DACA recipients; meets full demonstrated need.

sources.name: MIT CDS 2024-25
sources.evidence: Overall admit rate 4.52%; EA admit rate 5.17%; first-gen ~17% of class with admit rate inferred ~7-9%.

sources.name: Common App Undocumented Applicant Brief 2024
sources.evidence: Undocumented applicants are admitted at need-blind T20s (MIT, Harvard, Princeton, Yale, Stanford, Amherst, Pomona, Bowdoin, Williams) at rates comparable to domestic peers controlling for academic strength.

sources.name: Crimson First-Gen STEM Report 2024
sources.evidence: First-gen + USACO Gold + research at T5 STEM schools cluster 10-25% admit rate; undocumented status itself is policy-neutral at MIT (no admit-rate penalty when school is need-blind-for-undocumented).
